_what: The journey kit's settings (do-work/journey.mjs): the visitor cookie a site's server sets, the URL parameters kept with a visit (the click id names come from ad-return.json, not repeated here), the step kinds a journey is written in, how a step is joined to a person, and the limits of the checkout fields Stripe reads. Each step kind's words are what it means in plain speech. Code reads these names and never branches on a client, a site or a provider.

cookie.name: jv
cookie._what: Set by the server, so Safari's 7-day limit on script-set cookies does not apply. HttpOnly: the page script never reads it. The value is random and carries nothing about the person.

_kept_params_what: URL parameters a visit keeps as its source. t is the touch id a /go/ link sends the visitor on with. The ad click ids are added from ad-return.json's click_ids.
_retry_after_seconds_what: Retry-After sent with a 503 when the database cannot be reached for a /go/ link.

beacon._what: A static page (served without the program) loads this script; it posts the page's own address to the beacon route, which keeps the visit. The route ignores foreign origins and bodies over max_bytes.

consent._what: Without analytics consent a site keeps no visitor cookie and no visitor id: a step keeps only the touch id of the link it followed.

_touch_param_what: The URL parameter that carries the touch id from a /go/ redirect to the destination page.

touch.words: A tracked link was made for a post, ad, email or bio

click.words: A visitor followed a tracked link

visit.words: A visitor loaded a page that came with a source

lead.words: A visitor gave their details or asked to hear more

booking.words: A visitor booked a call or a session

checkout.words: A visitor opened a payment page

product.words: A paid product was handed over to the buyer

cookie.words: The step carries the visitor's cookie

touch.words: The step carries the touch id the visitor was sent on with

email.words: The step has only the email, made into email_key; it joins to a visitor who gave that email

client_reference_id.words: A payment carries the visitor id the checkout was opened with

self_reported.words: The visitor said where they heard about it

email_key.rule: lower(trim(email)) read as bytes, identity made by tools/content-identity (BLAKE3 of the exact bytes)
email_key._what: The only form of an email a journey keeps. The raw email is never written to journey_steps.

stripe._what: Stripe's documented limits for the fields a Checkout Session carries: client_reference_id, and metadata's key count, key length and value length.
stripe._offer_key_what: The metadata key a site sets to the offer a checkout sells, read back by saleStepOf.

tidycal._what: The post-booking redirect's query names. The site's /booked route reads them; the TidyCal template is https://<site>/booked?email={contact.email}&starts={booking.starts_at}&type={booking_type.title}. booking_key is read only when the template also sends the provider's booking id.
